messages:
Noah Patel: Quick question — I paid for a client dinner in Stockholm on my personal card. Receipt shows 1,120 SEK but the restaurant sent an invoice for 1,360 SEK citing a late service charge and a seating fee. Do we reimburse the card amount or try to have Accounting pay the vendor?
Rae (Finance): Hi Noah — can you attach the card receipt and the vendor invoice? If the invoice is addressed to Redwood AB with VAT ID we can vendor-pay; otherwise we'll reimburse you and chase the vendor for a corrected invoice.
Noah Patel: Uploading now (links). The invoice headers list "Redwood Inference AB" but the VAT number field is blank. Card charge is 1,120 SEK (shows tipping included).
AccountingBot: Files uploaded: receipt_noah_sthlm.jpg, rest_invoice_03-2026.pdf (https://files.redwood/receipts/noah_sthlm.jpg)
Rae (Finance): Thanks. Policy note: seating/cover fees are reimbursable if incurred by staff, but vendor must provide VAT info for company payment. If time critical, we reimburse the employee for 1,120 SEK. Manager approval required for full reconciliation.
Marta (Manager): I approve reimbursing Noah 1,120 SEK now. Finance, please request corrected VAT invoice from the restaurant for the additional 240 SEK.
Rae (Finance): Will do. Action: reimburse Noah 1,120 SEK (REF-FIN-3299). We'll email vendor requesting corrected invoice and hold additional payment until we receive it. Expected clearing: 2 business days.
Noah Patel: Thanks all — prefer SEK payout to my Swedbank acct (last 2 digits 44). I'll forward the booking confirmation to Rae.
Rae (Finance): Noted and queued. Thanks Noah.
